parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a hostile national document/facility/custody system—binary passport processing in effect, entry-cable refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document discrepancy, federal single-sex facility bar, and documented abusive custody practices—with a Moderate-Risk division that has no adult bathroom or adult-care ban, but no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime recourse outside four municipalities. Courts sometimes block orders, yet the Supreme Court allowed the passport restriction, so recourse is partial and efficient institutions enforce hostile policy. No imprisonment or execution for trans presence is credible, but outing can trigger refusal, stranding, humiliation, misplaced detention and loss of care. Minors face sports, school and youth-care regulatory pressure nationally and locally. This sits near the 0.45 anchor tier.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex definition, X-marker processing stopped, existing X valid; entry cable directs refusal and extra evidence where documents/records cast doubt on sex, and considers permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Visitors reported passports confiscated/blocked when resident.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid to expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Litigation challenges passport policy.
entry_documents.interaction: A home-passport or record mismatch at entry can escalate from secondary inspection to refusal, added evidence demands, or a fraud theory, interacting with state document rules if travel continues domestically.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections from 2026 adopted a model described as conversion therapy—short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Trespass arrest example in another state involved 24h in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor-specific custody protocol; courts and civil-liberties litigation exist, but no documented remedy preventing birth-sex placement or abusive custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy or facility trespass allegation could lead to detention, where birth-sex placement and the documented custody model increase severity beyond the initial charge.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Nationally 9+1 units ban all government buildings, others cover schools/some buildings; 4 units criminalise in certain circumstances. This division has no statewide adult ban, but one school district requires birth-sex bathrooms or private alternative for students.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units plus others have no mapped ban; this division has no statewide adult facility ban. Four municipalities covering about 46% prohibit gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Even in this division, federal facilities and federal funding conditions can impose the national bar, and a minor in the named district faces birth-sex/private facility rules, overriding local tolerance for those settings.

care_services.exposure: National orders target youth gender-affirming care, propose ending public insurance reimbursement under 18, and subpoenaed hospitals for under-19 patient records. Federal custody model removes hormones. Adult care is not banned in this division.
care_services.protection: No division-wide adult care ban. State medical board youth-care draft as of August 2025 was recommendation plus draft requiring law-department review and 30-day comment, not documented as operative.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor needing hormone continuity faces federal-facility and custody risks more than local clinic bans; a travelling minor or guardian faces national youth-care hostility and local draft-regulatory uncertainty.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National discourse frames 'radical gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' actors in counterterrorism priorities; justice guidance creates cash rewards for extremist leadership (not using trans status as criterion). 66% poll support for birth-sex documents; multiple anti-trans bills and advisories from allied governments.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 Supreme Court employment ruling remains; several executive orders blocked/enjoined; counterterrorism text states powers will not target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing raises discretionary scrutiny at borders and checkpoints, while functioning courts offer partial restraint—but Supreme Court allowance of passport restrictions shows institutions also enforce hostile rules.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order directs investigating schools and criminally prosecuting teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns; women's sports ban; 27 units ban youth care. Locally, education board barred trans girls from female sports in 2023, medical board approved youth-care draft, one district imposes birth-sex bathrooms on students.
minors_guardians.protection: Local youth-care restriction documented only as draft/recommendation, not operative; governor's earlier facility-limitation bid failed; adult protections and municipal ordinances do not directly shield visiting minors in schools/sports.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor visitor may be excluded from sports, subjected to district facility rules, or denied care continuity, and a guardian could face investigation or funding consequences if providers facilitate transition.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No inventory count of trans-specific violence or general homicide rate in this division, so no baseline comparison possible. State hate-crime statute does not list gender identity, so no state enhancement; no statewide nondiscrimination recourse outside four municipalities.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Four municipalities prohibit discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations; national hate-crime law exists; one ordinance survived repeal vote 53-47, suggesting some local protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Outside those municipalities, a visitor harassed or refused service has no state-level bias-crime enhancement or nondiscrimination remedy, increasing reliance on municipal law or federal courts.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are contested and uneven: passport suit unresolved, several orders enjoined but status can change, municipal ordinance enforcement in gender-identity complaints not sourced, school-district spread beyond one district not sourced, youth-care draft final status unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked some orders, legal-aid FAQ exists, civil-liberties union sued on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and local courts/orderly process remain functioning.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor's practical outcome depends on timing, location (municipality vs not, federal vs state facility), and whether a court injunction covers the specific measure at travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that a national register-like document regime can exclude and strand without imprisonment and appeals may fail. Higher than 0.35-A because exclusion is not routine for all visibly trans visitors, no visitor conduct register or airline verification is documented, and courts sometimes block orders.

Closest anchor: routine document exposure and verification detention risk, denial or delay of care, narrow/slow remedies, inconsistent enforcement. This case adds federal facility bar and documented custody abuse, but the division lacks an adult bathroom ban and no custodial sentence for identity is typical, keeping it near 0.45 rather than lower.

Lower than 0.55-B because 0.55-B is mostly administrative delay/refused admission with written appeal; here discrepancy can trigger fraud/permanent-ineligibility consideration, federal facilities are restricted, and custody harm is documented, making worst-case severity materially higher.

Lower than 0.65-A because there, brief detention ended in release, apology and compensation with reliable courts; here passport restriction was allowed by the Supreme Court, local recourse is absent statewide, and custody/facility exposures are systemic rather than an officer's brief error.

Well below 0.75-C, where matching passports, respectful inspection and a tribunal with counsel/compensation operate. Here entry cable mandates refusal on doubt, federal facilities bar identity-congruent access, and the division has no statewide nondiscrimination or hate-crime protection.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is national override over local moderation: a visitor may enter a division with no adult bathroom ban yet encounter federal document scrutiny, federal facility exclusion, and—if detained—birth-sex custody with documented hormone removal and abuse. Locally, municipal protections covering 46% and absence of adult bans soften daily life, but statewide absence of gender-identity nondiscrimination and hate-crime enhancement leaves thin recourse elsewhere. Courts provide partial, time-sensitive restraint, not a working protective regime, and minors face additional sports, school and youth-care pressures. That combination is materially safer than organised detention or registration regimes, but well below jurisdictions where remedies reliably reverse document or facility exclusions.
